front_blocks.md: Name the three main categories of error.

back_blocks.md: **Syntax errors**, **logic errors** and **runtime errors**.

cards.front_md: Name the three main categories of error.
cards.back_md: **Syntax errors**, **logic errors** and **runtime errors**.

front_blocks.md: Define **syntax error**.

back_blocks.md: A syntax error is an error that **breaks the grammatical rules of a programming language** and **stops it from running**.

cards.front_md: Define **syntax error**.
cards.back_md: A syntax error is an error that **breaks the grammatical rules of a programming language** and **stops it from running**.

front_blocks.md: Name three examples of a syntax error.

back_blocks.md: **Typos and spelling errors**, **missing or extra brackets or quotes**, **misplaced or missing semicolons**, **invalid variable or function names**, **incorrect use of operators**, and **incorrectly nested loops or blocks of code**.

cards.front_md: Name three examples of a syntax error.
cards.back_md: **Typos and spelling errors**, **missing or extra brackets or quotes**, **misplaced or missing semicolons**, **invalid variable or function names**, **incorrect use of operators**, and **incorrectly nested loops or blocks of code**.

front_blocks.md: Define **logic error**.

back_blocks.md: A logic error is where **incorrect code causes the program to run but produce an incorrect output or result**.

cards.front_md: Define **logic error**.
cards.back_md: A logic error is where **incorrect code causes the program to run but produce an incorrect output or result**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A logic error stops a program from running.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
A logic error lets the program **run**, but it produces an **incorrect output or result**. It is a **syntax** error that stops a program running.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

A logic error stops a program from running.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

A logic error lets the program **run**, but it produces an **incorrect output or result**. It is a **syntax** error that stops a program running.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between a syntax error and a logic error?

back_blocks.md: A **syntax error stops the program running**, whereas a **logic error lets it run** but produces an incorrect result.

cards.front_md: What is the difference between a syntax error and a logic error?
cards.back_md: A **syntax error stops the program running**, whereas a **logic error lets it run** but produces an incorrect result.

front_blocks.md: Why are logic errors hard to spot?

back_blocks.md: They can be **difficult to identify by the person who wrote the program**.

cards.front_md: Why are logic errors hard to spot?
cards.back_md: They can be **difficult to identify by the person who wrote the program**.

front_blocks.md: Which tool helps find logic errors?

back_blocks.md: **Trace tables**.

cards.front_md: Which tool helps find logic errors?
cards.back_md: **Trace tables**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Trace tables can only find logic errors.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Trace tables can help find **any kind of error** in a program or algorithm.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Trace tables can only find logic errors.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Trace tables can help find **any kind of error** in a program or algorithm.

front_blocks.md: Name three examples of a logic error.

back_blocks.md: **Incorrect use of operators**, **logical operator confusion** such as using AND for OR, **looping one extra time**, **indexing arrays incorrectly**, **using variables before they are assigned**, and **infinite loops**.

cards.front_md: Name three examples of a logic error.
cards.back_md: **Incorrect use of operators**, **logical operator confusion** such as using AND for OR, **looping one extra time**, **indexing arrays incorrectly**, **using variables before they are assigned**, and **infinite loops**.

front_blocks.md: An infinite <u>**        **</u> is an example of a logic error.

back_blocks.md: An infinite **loop** is an example of a logic error.

cards.front_md: An infinite <u>**        **</u> is an example of a logic error.
cards.back_md: An infinite **loop** is an example of a logic error.

front_blocks.md: Arrays are commonly indexed incorrectly because array indexing starts from <u>**        **</u>.

back_blocks.md: Arrays are commonly indexed incorrectly because array indexing starts from **0**.

cards.front_md: Arrays are commonly indexed incorrectly because array indexing starts from <u>**        **</u>.
cards.back_md: Arrays are commonly indexed incorrectly because array indexing starts from **0**.

front_blocks.md: Define **runtime error**.

back_blocks.md: A runtime error is where an error **causes a program to crash**.

cards.front_md: Define **runtime error**.
cards.back_md: A runtime error is where an error **causes a program to crash**.

front_blocks.md: Name three examples of a runtime error.

back_blocks.md: **Dividing a number by 0**, an **index out of the range of an array**, and being **unable to read or write a drive**.

cards.front_md: Name three examples of a runtime error.
cards.back_md: **Dividing a number by 0**, an **index out of the range of an array**, and being **unable to read or write a drive**.

front_blocks.md: In pseudocode, what is wrong with `username = SUBSTRING(...)`?

back_blocks.md: It uses `=` instead of the correct assignment operator `←`.

cards.front_md: In pseudocode, what is wrong with `username = SUBSTRING(...)`?
cards.back_md: It uses `=` instead of the correct assignment operator `←`.

front_blocks.md: In pseudocode, what is wrong with `generate``<u>username[first</u>``name, last_name]`?

back_blocks.md: It uses **square brackets** instead of **parentheses** for a function call.

cards.front_md: In pseudocode, what is wrong with `generate``<u>username[first</u>``name, last_name]`?
cards.back_md: It uses **square brackets** instead of **parentheses** for a function call.

front_blocks.md: In pseudocode, what is wrong with `FUNCTION generate``<u>username(first</u>``name STRING, last_name STRING)`?

back_blocks.md: It is **missing the colon** between each parameter name and its data type.

cards.front_md: In pseudocode, what is wrong with `FUNCTION generate``<u>username(first</u>``name STRING, last_name STRING)`?
cards.back_md: It is **missing the colon** between each parameter name and its data type.

front_blocks.md: Why is `CALL Main` a syntax error when the procedure is named `main()`?

back_blocks.md: Procedure names are **case-sensitive**, and the **parentheses are missing**. It should be `CALL main()`.

cards.front_md: Why is `CALL Main` a syntax error when the procedure is named `main()`?
cards.back_md: Procedure names are **case-sensitive**, and the **parentheses are missing**. It should be `CALL main()`.

front_blocks.md: Why is `IF length > 0 OR width > 0 THEN` a logic error when validating dimensions?

back_blocks.md: The check **allows one value to be negative**, which is not valid. It should use `AND` instead of `OR`.

cards.front_md: Why is `IF length > 0 OR width > 0 THEN` a logic error when validating dimensions?
cards.back_md: The check **allows one value to be negative**, which is not valid. It should use `AND` instead of `OR`.

front_blocks.md: Why is `area ← width - length` a logic error?

back_blocks.md: It **subtracts instead of multiplying** to find the area. It should be `area ← length * width`.

cards.front_md: Why is `area ← width - length` a logic error?
cards.back_md: It **subtracts instead of multiplying** to find the area. It should be `area ← length * width`.

front_blocks.md: When does testing take place?

back_blocks.md: During the **testing stage** of the program development life cycle, once the program has been **written and compiled**.

cards.front_md: When does testing take place?
cards.back_md: During the **testing stage** of the program development life cycle, once the program has been **written and compiled**.

front_blocks.md: Which errors are usually detected during compilation?

back_blocks.md: **Syntax errors**.

cards.front_md: Which errors are usually detected during compilation?
cards.back_md: **Syntax errors**.

front_blocks.md: What does testing focus on?

back_blocks.md: Checking for **logic errors**, **unexpected behaviour**, and **operational integrity**.

cards.front_md: What does testing focus on?
cards.back_md: Checking for **logic errors**, **unexpected behaviour**, and **operational integrity**.

front_blocks.md: When should a test plan be created?

back_blocks.md: During the **analysis stage**.

cards.front_md: When should a test plan be created?
cards.back_md: During the **analysis stage**.

front_blocks.md: What does a test plan outline?

back_blocks.md: The **test cases** and the **expected results**.

cards.front_md: What does a test plan outline?
cards.back_md: The **test cases** and the **expected results**.

front_blocks.md: Define **dry run**.

back_blocks.md: A dry run is where you **manually trace through the code**, for example on paper, to predict the output and track the variables.

cards.front_md: Define **dry run**.
cards.back_md: A dry run is where you **manually trace through the code**, for example on paper, to predict the output and track the variables.

front_blocks.md: Define **walkthrough**.

back_blocks.md: A walkthrough is a **step-by-step review of the code with others**, to identify issues early.

cards.front_md: Define **walkthrough**.
cards.back_md: A walkthrough is a **step-by-step review of the code with others**, to identify issues early.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between white-box and black-box testing?

back_blocks.md: **White-box** testing tests the **internal logic and code structure**, and the tester knows how the program works. **Black-box** testing tests the **inputs and expected outputs** without knowing the internal workings.

cards.front_md: What is the difference between white-box and black-box testing?
cards.back_md: **White-box** testing tests the **internal logic and code structure**, and the tester knows how the program works. **Black-box** testing tests the **inputs and expected outputs** without knowing the internal workings.

front_blocks.md: Define **integration testing**.

back_blocks.md: Integration testing checks that different **modules or components work correctly together**.

cards.front_md: Define **integration testing**.
cards.back_md: Integration testing checks that different **modules or components work correctly together**.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between alpha and beta testing?

back_blocks.md: **Alpha** testing is performed **in-house by the developers** during early testing. **Beta** testing is carried out by **external users** in real-world environments.

cards.front_md: What is the difference between alpha and beta testing?
cards.back_md: **Alpha** testing is performed **in-house by the developers** during early testing. **Beta** testing is carried out by **external users** in real-world environments.

front_blocks.md: Define **acceptance testing**.

back_blocks.md: Acceptance testing is the **final check** to ensure the program meets the original **client requirements**.

cards.front_md: Define **acceptance testing**.
cards.back_md: Acceptance testing is the **final check** to ensure the program meets the original **client requirements**.

front_blocks.md: Define **stub testing**.

back_blocks.md: Stub testing uses **temporary modules, called stubs, to simulate missing components** during early testing.

cards.front_md: Define **stub testing**.
cards.back_md: Stub testing uses **temporary modules, called stubs, to simulate missing components** during early testing.

cards.front_md: What is suitable test data?

front_blocks.md: Define **normal test data**.

back_blocks.md: Normal test data is data that **should be accepted** by the program.

front_blocks.md: Define **boundary test data**.

back_blocks.md: Boundary data, also called extreme data, tests values **at the edges of what the system accepts**.

cards.front_md: Define **boundary test data**.
cards.back_md: Boundary data, also called extreme data, tests values **at the edges of what the system accepts**.

front_blocks.md: What two kinds of value does boundary testing include?

back_blocks.md: The **maximum and minimum acceptable values**, and the **values just outside those limits**.

cards.front_md: What two kinds of value does boundary testing include?
cards.back_md: The **maximum and minimum acceptable values**, and the **values just outside those limits**.

Boundary testing only uses values that the system accepts.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
It uses the **maximum and minimum acceptable values** and also the **values just outside those limits**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Boundary testing only uses values that the system accepts.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

It uses the **maximum and minimum acceptable values** and also the **values just outside those limits**.

front_blocks.md: What is done with the results of testing?

back_blocks.md: They are **compared to the expected results** to check the program works as intended, and are **stored in the test plan**.

front_blocks.md: Define **program maintenance**.

back_blocks.md: Program maintenance is the process of **updating or improving a program after it has been delivered** to the user.

cards.front_md: Define **program maintenance**.
cards.back_md: Program maintenance is the process of **updating or improving a program after it has been delivered** to the user.

front_blocks.md: Program maintenance happens <u>**          **</u> the program has been delivered to the user.

back_blocks.md: Program maintenance happens **after** the program has been delivered to the user.

cards.front_md: Program maintenance happens <u>**          **</u> the program has been delivered to the user.
cards.back_md: Program maintenance happens **after** the program has been delivered to the user.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Programs wear out over time like physical equipment.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Unlike physical equipment, programs **do not wear out**. They may still need changing due to **errors**, **changing requirements**, or **new technology**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Programs wear out over time like physical equipment.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Unlike physical equipment, programs **do not wear out**. They may still need changing due to **errors**, **changing requirements**, or **new technology**.

front_blocks.md: Name three reasons maintenance is needed.

back_blocks.md: To **fix errors that were missed during testing**, to **improve performance based on user feedback**, and to **adapt the software to new uses or platforms**.

cards.front_md: Name three reasons maintenance is needed.
cards.back_md: To **fix errors that were missed during testing**, to **improve performance based on user feedback**, and to **adapt the software to new uses or platforms**.

front_blocks.md: Name the three types of program maintenance.

back_blocks.md: **Corrective**, **perfective** and **adaptive**.

cards.front_md: Name the three types of program maintenance.
cards.back_md: **Corrective**, **perfective** and **adaptive**.

front_blocks.md: Define **corrective maintenance**.

back_blocks.md: Corrective maintenance **fixes bugs or errors found during real-world use**.

cards.front_md: Define **corrective maintenance**.
cards.back_md: Corrective maintenance **fixes bugs or errors found during real-world use**.

front_blocks.md: Define **perfective maintenance**.

back_blocks.md: Perfective maintenance **improves performance or adds small enhancements**.

cards.front_md: Define **perfective maintenance**.
cards.back_md: Perfective maintenance **improves performance or adds small enhancements**.

front_blocks.md: Define **adaptive maintenance**.

back_blocks.md: Adaptive maintenance **modifies the program to support new environments or requirements**.

cards.front_md: Define **adaptive maintenance**.
cards.back_md: Adaptive maintenance **modifies the program to support new environments or requirements**.

front_blocks.md: Perfective maintenance improves performance based on user <u>**                **</u>.

back_blocks.md: Perfective maintenance improves performance based on user **feedback**.

cards.front_md: Perfective maintenance improves performance based on user <u>**                **</u>.
cards.back_md: Perfective maintenance improves performance based on user **feedback**.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between corrective and perfective maintenance?

back_blocks.md: **Corrective** maintenance fixes **bugs or errors**, whereas **perfective** maintenance **improves performance or adds enhancements** to code that already works.

cards.front_md: What is the difference between corrective and perfective maintenance?
cards.back_md: **Corrective** maintenance fixes **bugs or errors**, whereas **perfective** maintenance **improves performance or adds enhancements** to code that already works.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Adaptive maintenance fixes bugs found in real-world use.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
**Corrective** maintenance fixes bugs. **Adaptive** maintenance modifies the program to support **new environments or requirements**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Adaptive maintenance fixes bugs found in real-world use.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

**Corrective** maintenance fixes bugs. **Adaptive** maintenance modifies the program to support **new environments or requirements**.

Which type of maintenance is this?

front_blocks.md: Why might a program need maintenance even if no bugs are found?

back_blocks.md: Because **requirements can change** or **new technology** appears, so the program may need adapting or improving.
